findings: 2026-11-06: drafted for Mathematics 12 Unit 3 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: The book prints "In terms of definite integrals \int F'(g(x))\,g'(x) = F(g(x)) + c". It should say indefinite integrals (a definite integral has limits and no +\,c), and the dx is missing. Correct: \int F'(g(x))\,g'(x)\,dx = F(g(x)) + c.

Book correction: The theorem's formula is printed as \int f(g(x)\cdot g'(x)dx = F(u) + c: a bracket is missing and the result uses u before u has been defined. Correct: \int f(g(x))\,g'(x)\,dx = F(g(x)) + c. Only after letting u = g(x) does it become \int f(u)\,du = F(u) + c.
